question: the peer measured the candidate oracle's training activity distribution over all 798,064 rows and assigned the comparison: does our corpus's activity distribution differ from it?
ANSWER: THE COMPARISON CANNOT RUN AS FRAMED. Our activity values are per-cell STANDARDISED while the oracle's are raw log2 fold-change, so the two are not on a common scale and no difference between them is interpretable as a distribution shift. On the one statistic that survives rescaling, the two AGREE.

THE_SUBSTRATE_FACT_WORTH_CARRYING.finding: Table S6's activity column is labelled 'Observed log2(RNA/DNA)' and the loader carries that label faithfully, but the values are PER-CELL STANDARDISED: mean 0 and sample sd exactly 1.0 in all three cells.
THE_SUBSTRATE_FACT_WORTH_CARRYING.mechanism_proved_not_asserted: a sd of 'about 1' could be coincidence. The POPULATION sd is not 1 -- it is sqrt((n-1)/n), because the publishers divided by the SAMPLE sd (ddof=1). Predicted from n ALONE and compared against the measured value, the residual is 1.11e-16 (HepG2, n=61,463), 0 (K562, n=98,332) and 1.11e-16 (WTC11, n=23,064) -- machine precision, in three cells of DIFFERENT size. A coincidence cannot track n.
THE_SUBSTRATE_FACT_WORTH_CARRYING.who_is_wrong: not the loader. The publishers' own column label understates the transform; our loader reproduces the label and the values verbatim.

THE_FALSE_POSITIVE_THIS_PREVENTED.what_the_naive_comparison_says: our median is -0.19 / -0.23 / -0.27 against the oracle's 0.17-0.20, so the naive reading is 'our corpus is systematically LESS ACTIVE than the data the oracle was trained on' -- a confident distribution-shift claim, with numbers, that would have argued against adopting the oracle on grounds that do not exist.
THE_FALSE_POSITIVE_THIS_PREVENTED.why_it_is_false: a standardised distribution has mean 0 BY CONSTRUCTION and a right-skewed one then has a negative median by construction. The sign carries no information about activity.
THE_FALSE_POSITIVE_THIS_PREVENTED.frac_gt_1_is_the_same_trap_under_one_nam: ours 0.164-0.165, theirs 0.19-0.20, which looks like a mild difference. It is not a comparison at all: for us the threshold 1 is ONE STANDARD DEVIATION, for them it is ONE LOG2 UNIT of fold change. Same name, different quantity -- the shape this repo has already recorded for a sensitivity matching a specificity of equal value.

oracle_reference_quoted_not_reproduced.source: peer measurement over all 798,064 rows of the oracle's own training table, 0 non-numeric cells; quoted as across-cell ranges as reported

WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_IT_AGREES.statistic: nonparametric skew = (mean - median) / sd, invariant under positive affine rescaling
WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_IT_AGREES.reading: on the one statistic the two conventions cannot distort, the distributions are comparable: both are right-skewed by a similar amount. So there is no evidence of an activity-distribution shift -- which leaves the peer's SELECTION-criterion difference (98.23% variant-centred vs our cCRE/DNase/TSS) standing on its own, unsupported by and unrefuted by activity.
WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_IT_AGREES.SUPERSEDED: this block reasons from a BOUND [0.192, 0.318] built out of across-cell ranges, and its own key name asserts agreement. Exact per-cell values have since replaced the bound and both matched pairs point the SAME way, so the agreement reading does NOT hold. Read REVISED_SKEW_ON_EXACT_VALUES instead; this is kept for provenance, not as a conclusion.

CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_ORACLE_DECISION: the peer's SELECTION-criterion difference stands on its own and is unaffected: the oracle's training rows are 98.23% variant-centred (GTEX 55.83% + UKBB 42.40%) against 1.77% element-selected, while our corpus is cCRE / DNase / TSS-selected throughout. What this measurement adds is that activity neither supports NOR refutes a shift -- so the distribution-matching argument for fitting our own head rests on the selection criterion alone, not on an activity difference. Anyone citing an activity gap would be citing an artifact.
none_of_todays_published_numbers_depend_: the oracle gate is Spearman, which is rank-based and invariant under any monotone transform, so standardisation cannot move it. The WTC11 figures (0.3607 best arm against a GC baseline of 0.0858) are unaffected either way.
honest_limits: The oracle's skew is BOUNDED from across-cell ranges, not computed per cell, because that is how it was reported -- so the overlap is a bound, not a per-cell match.
Nonparametric skew is one scale-free summary. Two distributions can share it and still differ in shape; this does not establish the distributions are the same.
A rank-based oracle metric (Spearman) is unaffected by standardisation either way, so none of today's published oracle figures depend on which convention holds.
That the values are standardised is inferred from mean 0 / sd 1 at 1e-9 across three independent cells, not from a statement by the publishers.

The oracle's activity reference is the peer's measurement, quoted and NOT reproduced here; its skew is therefore bounded from across-cell ranges rather than computed per cell, so the overlap is a bound and not a per-cell match.

A scale bridge would settle it properly: the 100 sequences present in BOTH datasets have one true activity each, so comparing them pairwise separates convention from shift. That needs the oracle's per-sequence values, which the hash sets do not carry. Those 100 are also promoter-enriched 2.17x, so they would bound rather than settle it.

supersedes.why_an_edit_and_not_an_addition: the previous verdict asserted SKEW_AGREES, which a reader takes as the answer. It was computed from a BOUND because only across-cell ranges were available; the data owner has since supplied exact per-cell values. Recomputing on better input is not goalpost-moving -- and it weakens my own conclusion rather than strengthening it, so leaving the old string live would have left a false claim at the top of the record.

REVISED_SKEW_ON_EXACT_VALUES.CORRECTION_1_THERE_ARE_TWO_MATCHED_PAIRS: three values were reported on each side, which invites a three-pair reading. It is not: the oracle's third cell is SKNSH (neuroblastoma) and ours is WTC11 (iPSC). DIFFERENT CELL LINES, so they do not pair. Two matched pairs only, which cuts an already-tiny n by a third. Raised by the peer session and accepted.

unpaired_and_reported_rather_than_droppe.note: neither has a counterpart; listed so the pairing is auditable

REVISED_SKEW_ON_EXACT_VALUES.CORRECTION_2_MY_NEGATIVE_WAS_UNDERPOWERE: the range-overlap statement concealed a consistent direction: in BOTH matched pairs the oracle side is more right-skewed. 'No evidence either way' was therefore the wrong framing -- the right one is NO RESOLVABLE DIFFERENCE AT THIS POWER, WITH A CONSISTENT BUT UNPOWERED DIRECTION. Two pairs cannot resolve a skew difference. Raised by the peer and accepted; it is the same correction this project applied to the tokenization null, that an underpowered negative is not an absence.

CORRECTION_3_THE_PAIRING_AS_RECEIVED_WAS.what_happened: the correction arrived pairing oracle K562 0.2838 against 0.1927 and oracle HepG2 0.2577 against 0.2250 -- but 0.1927 is OUR HEPG2 and 0.2250 is OUR K562, so the two cell lines were swapped. The arithmetic was right; the pairing was not.
CORRECTION_3_THE_PAIRING_AS_RECEIVED_WAS.consequence_and_it_runs_AGAINST_my_inter: corrected, the deltas are HepG2 +0.0650 (1.337x) and K562 +0.0588 (1.261x), which agree with each other within 11%% -- not the reported 4.5x divergence (which does not follow even from the crossed numbers, those giving 2.79x). So the consistent-direction finding is STRONGER than as received, not weaker: same direction AND closely similar magnitude across two independent cell lines. That makes my original verdict more wrong, not less.

REVISED_SKEW_ON_EXACT_VALUES.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_REINSTATE: nothing. Skew is distribution SHAPE, not activity LEVEL, so even a fully powered skew difference would not be an activity shift -- and the scale mismatch that voids the level comparison is untouched by any of this. The narrowing stands exactly as committed: the SELECTION-criterion finding (98.23%% variant-centred against our cCRE/DNase/TSS selection) is the distribution-matching case for fitting our own head, and it stands ALONE. One argument, not two converging ones.

oracle_exact_values_now_available.source: peer session, computed from its stored figures with no re-stream; supersedes the across-cell ranges from which [0.192, 0.318] was bounded here

honest_limits: Two matched cell lines. A consistent direction across two pairs is suggestive, NOT a powered estimate, and must not be quoted as a measured skew difference.
Nonparametric skew is one scale-free summary; agreement or disagreement on it does not establish that the distributions match or differ in shape generally.
Our values are standardised and the oracle's are raw, which skew tolerates by construction -- but that tolerance is exactly why skew cannot speak to activity LEVEL.

supersedes.why: the previous string said UNPOWERED, which is measurably wrong about the per-cell difference and puts the uncertainty in the wrong place. Corrected on measurement, one commit after writing it.

WHERE_THE_UNCERTAINTY_ACTUALLY_LIVES.measured: bootstrap standard error of nonparametric skew, 200 resamples per cell: 0.00243 (HepG2, n=61,463) and 0.00218 (K562, n=98,332). The oracle-minus-ours offsets of +0.0650 and +0.0588 are therefore 26.7 and 26.9 standard errors. The oracle side carries an even smaller error on ~440k rows, so the difference SE is dominated by ours.
WHERE_THE_UNCERTAINTY_ACTUALLY_LIVES.consequence_1_the_offset_is_NOT_noise: at n in the tens of thousands each skew is pinned to about +/-0.002, so MEASUREMENT noise was never the binding limit and the 10.5% magnitude concordance is NOT evidence against it -- there was no meaningful noise to rule out. In each of the two matched cells the difference is statistically unambiguous.
WHERE_THE_UNCERTAINTY_ACTUALLY_LIVES.consequence_2_so_UNPOWERED_was_the_wrong: the per-cell difference IS resolved. What two pairs cannot establish is (a) that it GENERALISES beyond these two cell lines, and (b) its CAUSE -- the two corpora differ in element selection (variant-centred vs cCRE/DNase/TSS) AND in assay and lab, and two pairs cannot separate those. That is where the uncertainty lives.
WHERE_THE_UNCERTAINTY_ACTUALLY_LIVES.the_firewall_is_UNCHANGED_by_this: skew is distribution SHAPE, not activity LEVEL. A real, precisely-measured, 27-SE skew offset is still not an activity shift, and the scale mismatch voiding the level comparison is untouched. The selection-criterion finding remains the sole distribution-matching argument. Nothing here reinstates an activity claim.
honest_limits: The bootstrap is on OUR values only; the oracle SE is inferred from its row count, not measured.
Two cell lines. Precision within a cell says nothing about generality across cells.
Selection and assay/lab are confounded across the two corpora and cannot be separated here.
